title: kiln.json
description: kiln.json is kiln's settings for a project, in .kiln/kiln.json. kiln reads them from main, never from a build's checkout, so a build cannot weaken its own gate.

$schema.description: $schema is the path of the JSON Schema that an editor checks this file against: "./generated/kiln.schema.json". kiln init writes that schema to .kiln/generated/. kiln ignores this key.

gate.description: gate lists the commands that must pass before work lands on main, such as ["go vet ./...", "go test ./..."]. kiln runs each with sh -c, from the top of a checkout of the work. kiln refuses a kiln.json that lists no command.

rounds.description: rounds is how many times kiln sends a build back to its session before the build stops, such as 3. kiln sends a build back when its gate fails, its work conflicts with main, or its work changes nothing. The audit's findings go back too, and use no round. Absent or 0, the first failing gate stops the build.

allowedHosts.description: allowedHosts lists the only hosts that a session's shell commands may connect to, such as ["proxy.golang.org", "*.example.org"]. Write each as a bare host name, with no scheme, port or path. Absent, a session's shell commands connect to no host.

allowUnixSockets.description: allowUnixSockets lets a session's shell commands connect to and listen on any Unix socket, when true. Set it for a tool that opens a Unix socket, such as GoLand, which opens one as it starts. A Unix socket can reach a local service outside Claude Code's sandbox, such as Docker. Absent or false, the sandbox refuses each Unix socket.

writablePathCommands.description: writablePathCommands lists shell commands that print paths, such as ["go env GOCACHE GOMODCACHE"]. A session's shell commands may write to each printed path, as well as to the session's checkout. kiln runs each listed command with sh -c. kiln reads each word that the command prints as one absolute path. No session starts while a listed command fails, or prints a path that is not absolute. Absent, a session's shell commands write only to the session's checkout.

mcpServers.description: mcpServers lists the only MCP servers a session may call, by name, such as {"docs": {"command": "docs-mcp"}}. Write each server as Claude Code's own mcpServers setting holds one. Each server runs outside the sandbox that confines a session's shell commands. Absent, a session calls no MCP server.

workflow.description: workflow is how kiln builds a spec: "build", "build-and-verify" or "verify-first". Absent or "build", one build session writes the code and the acceptance tests. Otherwise a verify session writes the acceptance tests from the spec alone, and a build session writes the code. kiln proves the tests fail on main before the build session reads them. "build-and-verify" starts both sessions at once. "verify-first" starts the build session once the tests are proved. The verify session never reads the build session's work. A build uses the value that main held when the build was queued.

acceptanceTests.description: acceptanceTests is the path that holds a spec's acceptance tests, such as "uat/{spec}/". kiln puts the spec's name in place of {spec}. A list of such paths gives each spec several paths. Each path holds some text before {spec}. No listed path's text before {spec} starts with another's. kiln queue refuses every spec while acceptanceTests is absent. A build uses the value that main held when the build was queued.

testHelpers.description: testHelpers lists paths of helper code that the acceptance tests call, such as ["internal/testutil/"]. A verify session may write these paths, besides the acceptance tests and the spec's amendment file. The build session may write these paths too. kiln queue refuses a spec whose acceptance path equals, holds or lies under one of these paths. A build uses the value that main held when the build was queued.

testFiles.description: testFiles lists patterns that name the project's test files, such as ["*_test.go", "testdata"]. A file is a test file when a pattern matches an element of its path, by Go's path.Match. A pattern holds no slash. In a monitor whose workflow is "build-and-verify" or "verify-first", the files under testHelpers are test files too. So are the files under each acceptanceTests path's part before {spec}. Such a monitor's verify session writes only test files, and its fix session writes none. Absent, kiln refuses each such monitor.

reaudit.description: reaudit lists paths whose changes the audit must read before the work lands, such as ["migrations/"]. The audit reads the work once. When the work changes one of these paths after that, the audit reads the work again. That second reading uses a round. Absent, the audit never reads what a session changes in answer to the audit's findings.

notify.description: notify is a command that receives each notification, such as ".kiln/notify". A notification says that a build or a fix needs the developer. The command runs with sh -c, and reads the notification as JSON from the environment variable KILN_NOTICE. kiln kills a command that runs past 30 seconds. Absent, or when the command fails, kiln prints the notification as an OSC 9 escape sequence. A terminal shows that sequence as a desktop notification.

timeout.description: timeout is how long one command that kiln runs for the project may take, such as one gate command. It is also how long a session may print nothing. Past it, kiln kills that command or session. It does not limit a whole build. Write a Go duration above zero, such as "2h". Absent, it is 1 hour.
